newsitem.title: USA: Mich. School Bond Loan Fund 'AA' affirmed - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Mich. School Bond Loan Fund 'AA' affirmed - S&P.

text.p: Standard & Poor's has affirmed the AA rating for $930.736 million of "qualified" debt of 128 issuers participating in the Michigan School Bond Loan Fund Program, the rating agency said in its CreditWeek Municipal publication this week.

The 42-year-old program provides qualifying districts with assistance in paying debt service and avoiding default. As a result, the program carries Michigan's AA rating and stable outlook, moving in tandem with any future state action, S&P said.

S&P has rated $3.94 billion of qualified debt of 227 participants in the program overall. Michigan school districts had $6.262 billion of qualified debt outstanding at the end of last year, S&P noted.
Twenty state have credit enhancement programs, which carry S&P ratings from A-minus to AAA depending on their structure, S&P noted.
